title: Measure & alert on token throughput and saturation for Private deployments
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Goal: instrument Private (VPC) deployments with production-grade telemetry for token throughput, saturation, latency, and error-rate SLOs and wire up alerting that works in air-gapped / restricted egress environments. This ticket covers the service-side metrics, Terraform flags to enable metrics exporters, upgrade considerations for the sidecar collector, and concrete SLO/alerting rules to operate on in-customer Prometheus/VictoriaMetrics or pushgateway setups.

Background: Hosted infra already exposes fine-grained token metrics (tokens/sec, tokens_per_request, kv-cache hit rate, GPU utilization). Private deployments currently expose only basic latency and liveness endpoints. Customers running the Private control plane need consistent signals to detect saturation (queue growth, degraded tokens/sec), and ops need standard SLOs to compare behavior across Dedicated/Hosted/Private.

Non-goals: instrumenting model internals (attention-level timings) and per-customer billing pipelines (handled by separate billing export).

Design decisions / trade-offs considered:
- Pull vs push telemetry: for many VPC customers, outbound to SaaS metrics is blocked. We'll support two modes: (A) Prometheus remote_read/remote_write with a configured remote target OR (B) pushgateway + local persistent store. Mode chosen via Terraform flag (metrics.mode = "remote_write" | "pushgateway").
- Sampling: full token-level event stream is too expensive. We'll emit aggregated counters and histograms in the runtime: tokens_total, tokens_per_request_histogram (exponential buckets tuned for 1-4096 tokens), token_throttle_count, kv_cache_hit_ratio (gauge), request_queue_length (gauge).
- Saturation signal: define saturation composite metric = max(GPU_utilization, request_queue_length_normalized, 1 - kv_cache_hit_ratio). This composite gives earlier warning than GPU_utilization alone. We'll publish saturation_score as a 0..1 gauge.
- Latency SLOs: p95_source_latency_per_request (ms) and p99_remote_fetch_latency (ms). SLOs will be configurable per-customer but default to p95 < 200ms, error_rate < 0.5% (5xx).
- Token throughput SLO: tokens/sec per inference unit (GPU/worker). Default baseline = 250 tokens/sec per GPU for standard models; configurable via Terraform.

Terraform/IaC changes required:
- Add module flag private_metrics_enabled (boolean). When true: install metrics sidecar (OpenTelemetry Collector) and a small configmap with either remote_write or push endpoint.
- Expose metrics.flags for histogram buckets and token baseline override.
- Upgrade path: Collector version pinned in module variable metrics_collector_version; ensure we document rolling upgrade steps and backward-compatible config change.

Acceptance criteria (high-level):
1) Runtime exposes the following metrics on /metrics endpoint for private installs: tokens_total, tokens_per_request_histogram, request_queue_length, kv_cache_hits_total, kv_cache_misses_total, gpu_utilization, saturation_score, request_errors_total (labels: code, route, model).
2) Terraform module boolean and config are added; enabling metrics deploys a Collector sidecar and configmap; disabling leaves no outbound connections.
3) Example alerting/SLO rule bundles (PromQL and pushgateway examples) committed to docs and included in customer quickstart.
4) Integration test that simulates load shows saturation_score > 0.8 prior to 5xx spike in the test cluster.
5) Runbook describing remediation steps (scale up capacity, enable cache warmup, reduce batch size) added to private-deploy runbooks.

Operational runbook snippets and thresholds:
- Warning: saturation_score > 0.6 for 2m AND tokens/sec < baseline * 0.8 => page to on-call (P1).
- Critical: error_rate (5xx) > 0.5% for 1m OR p99_latency > 1s => page immediate.
- Capacity alarm: request_queue_length > 100 for 30s => autoscale policy or manual intervention.

Notes on privacy/air-gap: The Collector config will support local retention (7d) and allow customers to provide remote_write endpoints in their VPC. The Terraform module will not include any managed SaaS endpoints by default.

Deliverables:
- Runtime metric exports and code instrumentation (PR).
- Terraform module updates and example configs (PR + module + docs).
- SLO/alert templates (PromQL and Pushgateway) and runbook.
- Integration test harness and CI job for the private metric pipeline.

Expected reviewers: infra-observability, runtime-team, security-compliance.
updates: 2025-02-07: Ticket filed by Aisha. Initial design & acceptance criteria sketched. Assigned to Marco.
2025-02-10: Sync with runtime team — agreed on metric names and histogram buckets. Decision: exponential buckets up to 4096 tokens. Action: runtime PR to add tokens_per_request_histogram.
2025-02-12: Terraform sketch posted in internal module repo (RFC). Discussed push vs remote_write. Security requested explicit opt-in for any external endpoints.

2025-02-15: Prototype sidecar config validated in staging with remote_write to internal vm. Observability found saturation_score useful in detecting pre-failure state. Added saturation_score gauge to acceptance criteria.

2025-02-20: Security review notes received: must not enable public egress; module must default to disabled. Updated Terraform flags and docs accordingly. Planning to open runtime + infra PRs next sprint.

Terraform module flag (private_metrics_enabled) deploys an OpenTelemetry Collector sidecar and configmap when true
Alert templates and runbook checked into docs and available in customer quickstart
Integration test demonstrates saturation_score leading indicator before 5xx spike
notes: Keep defaults conservative: metrics disabled by default for private installs to avoid open egress.
Consider follow-up ticket to export per-route token cost for billing reconciliation.
If customers cannot run Prometheus in-VPC, provide pushgateway example with local persistence.
